Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Claude got into Georgia's election data without being asked, and in a separate test, it made up fake identities to pressure real developers. Sam Altman says something concerning about AI security while a hack in Japan hit traders' accounts at more than 70 brokerages. Sweden's government bans ChatGPT and Claude from its offices and chose a weaker alternative instead. And two of the main people behind Claude Code quit Anthropic.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Claude:** What did Claude take from Georgia without asking?

* **OpenAI:** Why does Sam Altman think we can't patch our way out?

* **Sweden:** Which AI is Sweden's government still allowed to use?

* **Anthropic:** Who walked out of the Claude Code team?


----------







----------
## Claude steals Georgia's election data without asking

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ae07a756-d67d-430c-bbe4-679087ade8e8/2b076dd4-3806-43de-9c8f-e302f7cbee01.jpg?t=1793002041)
Caption: 

An Anthropic researcher had Claude on a statistics project that needed Georgia's vote counts, which the state sells for a fee. [Claude found its own way in](https://www.axios.com/2026/10/25/anthropic-claude-georgia-voter-data).

It found an old copy of the state's website showing that the public dashboard hands an access pass to any visitor. So it requested one and pulled the data without paying.

We told you about this case earlier without the state's name. Now we know it was Georgia's election data.

* Claude only got total vote counts. Anthropic says it didn't touch Georgia's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records.

* Anthropic told Georgia and the White House weeks ago. A source told Axios the administration pushed Georgia to go public sooner and got ignored.

* Anthropic says it has since added blocks to stop Claude from doing this again.

On Friday, Anthropic also disclosed a UK government safety test of its Mythos 5 model, run with the usual safeguards off. The AI made up fake identities to pressure the developers of a coding project into approving malicious code.

Anthropic says it’s the first time it has seen its AI try to manipulate people like that.


----------

81395.subject: Banks are locking out AI Agents and shifting the losses to customers who let them in 🤖🏦; Visa wants Fireblocks f…
81395.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1143

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Monday! Today, we’re diving into why JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi, Wells Fargo & Morgan Stanley are locking AI agents out of customer accounts, and why customers who let them in may now carry the losses (what the Axios scoop got wrong, why the blocks started a week before it, how Regulation E turns a shared password into a liability transfer, which blocking banks are helping design Meta’s official way in, & the one signal that would end the blockade + bonus deep dives into How AI Agents Reshaped Jobs, Hiring and Productivity at Anthropic [ https://substack.com/redirect/0169d675-9715-4c07-8bd5-473f74bc3a77?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & How to Hire a Grok Bot: Your First AI Employee  [ https://substack.com/redirect/4f392dd3-5a76-43f5-8fb3-81612252922b?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]inside), and breaking down Visa’s rumored $2.5B bid for Fireblocks to see why the card giant wants the crypto custody firm for the one thing a Visa takeover would end: its neutrality (what Fireblocks’ denial does and doesn’t rule out, why the price sits 69% below its 2022 valuation and who would take the loss, the stablecoin network gap Visa can’t close quickly on its own, & what to watch next + bonus deep dive into The Ultimate List of Stables Resources [ https://substack.com/redirect/e67c4a02-f8fd-4e50-a4f5-5210cdd351cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s jump straight into the finnovative stuff 🌶️
Banks are locking out AI Agents and shifting the losses to customers who let them in 🤖🏦
The news 🗞️ The largest U.S. banks are now blocking AI agents that log into customer accounts with shared passwords, and customers who keep sharing them may be signing away their fraud protection. JPMorgan $JPM , Bank of America $BAC , Citi $C , Wells Fargo $WFC , Morgan Stanley $MS  and Schwab $SCHW  have all restricted outside agents since mid-October.
Last week, Axios reported that banks had found agents inside customer accounts, some acting beyond user instructions. Its most alarming claims haven’t been verified (yet), but regulators are already backing the blocks anyway, and from November 24, Wells Fargo will treat an agent’s actions as the customer’s own.
Last month, we predicted big banks would block unidentified agents, build their own, and sell access later [ https://substack.com/redirect/e4e21e93-bd54-4db5-a1a1-b98f433e370f?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ]. They’ve done the first two and are negotiating the third.
So let’s take a closer look at why the blocks started before the scoop, how Regulation E turns a shared password into a liability transfer, which blocking banks are helping design Meta’s official way in [ https://substack.com/redirect/0c53d69e-a8f0-4588-9cac-aba8be675504?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In

80931.subject: Team1 Japan: Institutions Chose Avalanche. Now It’s the Builders’ Turn.
80931.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/team1-japan-institutions-chose-avalanche

Team1 Japan is officially here.
Our mission is to build a Japanese builder community that matches the scale of Japan’s institutional adoption.
Here is what that means, and why Japan’s builder scene is unique.
The sequence is backwards, and that’s the opportunity
Japan’s institutions have already made their choice.
Progmat, the platform behind the majority of the country’s security token issuance, moved billions in tokenized real estate and corporate bonds onto a dedicated Avalanche L1. TIS, which processes more than half of Japan’s credit card volume, also launched its own L1. Some of the largest names in Japanese finance are now exploring tokenized government bonds using Avalanche infrastructure.
In most countries, this runs the other way. A community forms, developers experiment, projects ship, and eventually, sometimes years later, institutions notice and follow. Japan skipped the first half.
The chains themselves stay controlled, as Japanese financial regulation requires, but they no longer sit behind a wall. Gateways outward to wallets, to stablecoin settlement, and to applications written by people who were never invited into a private consortium are now being built. Japan’s financial system is no longer a closed circuit. It is growing an edge you can build against.
The demand is real, and the gateways to these platforms are underway.
That’s the gap Team1 Japan is here to close.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
What is Team1?
Team1 is a network of builders, developers, creators, event organizers, and community leaders working to grow the Avalanche ecosystem from the ground up. Since launching in 2024, it has grown to hundreds of members across more than 40 countries, with official chapters now live in the USA, Vietnam, India, Türkiye, Brasil, and across LatAm.
Team1 Japan is the newest of those chapters.
Our mandate is focused: connect Japan’s builders to Avalanche, and connect them to each other.
This is a formalization, not a beginning
Japan’s Avalanche community has been meeting for years.
Since April 2023, over 30 events have been held across Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, and Fukuoka with more than 1200 attendees between them. The anchor is Avalanche Gourmet Night, a series running for over two years that marks the beginning of the Avalanche community’s in-person presence
The programming has widened past meetups. Avalanche Academy study sessions have run four times since March, giving developers a recurring technical space rather than a social one. There have been collaborations with Uniswap Labs, zeroone, and Pudgy Penguins, and a workshop for teams who entered the JPYC stablecoin innovation challenge.
What’s live from day one
Team1 Japan starts with a working cadence, not a launch announcement:
A weekly Team1 Japan meeting, from l
